title: Huskeys Raises $27M Series A Led by Blackstone to Tackle the Growing Complexity of Edge Security
partialText:
Cybersecurity is facing a new management problem at the network edge. Organizations now rely on an expanding combination of cloud providers, content delivery networks, web application firewalls and other edge services, creating fragmented environments that are increasingly difficult to understand and secure as a whole.

That challenge is becoming even more complicated as AI changes the nature of internet traffic. Autonomous agents are emerging as legitimate users of applications, while attackers are using AI-driven capabilities to identify and exploit vulnerabilities at greater speed and scale. Against that backdrop, Huskeys has raised a $27 million Series A led by Blackstone Innovations Investments, a development first reported by the Wall Street Journal, as the company looks to build a new category around managing security at the modern network edge.

The round brings Huskeys' total funding to $35 million, following an $8 million seed round. Other investors include Merlin Ventures, Skinos Ventures, Zscaler Ventures, Okta Ventures, Bright Pixel Capital and SV Angel, alongside individual investors including WAF and CAPTCHA inventor Eran Reshef and executives from organizations including Palo Alto Networks, Cloudflare, Check Point, AWS, Google, Microsoft and Intel.

The Network Edge Is Becoming a Management Challenge

The modern network edge has become a complex intersection of security, infrastructure and business operations. Applications are distributed across multiple environments and protected by different technologies, making it harder for security teams to determine whether controls are working effectively and whether changes can be made without disrupting legitimate traffic.

The consequences can be significant. Blocking the wrong traffic can mean lost customers and revenue, while allowing malicious traffic through can expose organizations to attacks. Security teams are increasingly expected to manage both risks simultaneously as applications become more dynamic and AI-driven.

AI is adding another layer of complexity. Autonomous agents are creating new forms of legitimate interaction with applications, while attackers are increasingly using AI-driven capabilities to accelerate the discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities. The result is a widening gap between the complexity of edge environments and the ability of organizations to manage them effectively.

Huskeys' response is a new category it calls Network Edge Security Management, or NESM.

Building a Unified Layer Across the Edge

Rather than asking organizations to replace their existing infrastructure, Huskeys is building a platform designed to operate on top of it. The company's Network Edge Security Management platform connects and orchestrates technologies across the modern network edge, including CDNs and WAFs, cloud-native security solutions, and network components such as load balancers, VPCs and security groups.

At the center of the platform is Huskeys' patented Unified Data Model, which creates a common layer of understanding across different environments, technologies and providers. The goal is to allow security insights, policies and actions to move across platforms while supporting multi-cloud and multi-vendor environments.

The platform includes capabilities such as continuous posture assessment, dynamic policy generation, orchestration and Virtual Patching. Virtual Patching is designed to help security teams mitigate vulnerabilities directly at the network edge within minutes while a permanent fix is developed, tested and deployed in application code.

The company is also focused on helping organizations identify and manage agentic traffic, enabling legitimate AI agents to interact with applications while reducing false positives and minimizing disruption to the business.

"We founded Huskeys because security teams are being asked to protect increasingly complex edge environments with legacy tools that were never designed to work together or to address the challenges of the new AI era," said Itai Gafni, CEO and Co-Founder of Huskeys. "Every business today runs through its network edge - that's where your customers, your revenue, and your threats all meet, yet for most organizations, that edge works against them instead of for them. As AI transforms both legitimate traffic and cyberattacks, organizations need an intelligence layer that continuously understands what’s happening across the edge and adapts security in real time. Our goal is to make the network finally work for the business, not against it. That’s the category we’re building.”

Blackstone Bets on a New Edge Security Category

Huskeys already counts TikTok, LEGOLAND, Ro, Blackstone and Hugging Face among its customer base. The company says it analyzes more than a trillion web requests and thousands of network configurations every day across organizations worldwide.

For Blackstone, the investment reflects a belief that the growing complexity of internet-facing applications requires a different approach to security management.

“The way organizations secure internet-facing applications is fundamentally changing. AI-driven traffic and increasingly fragmented edge environments require a new approach to security management,” said Adam Fletcher, Chief Information Security Officer at Blackstone. “Huskeys has built a platform designed to operate at enterprise scale while advancing a new category for the modern network edge. We believe the company is well positioned to redefine how organizations manage edge security, and we’re excited to support Huskeys as they continue to develop their product in this important category.”

As organizations continue to add cloud services, edge technologies and AI-driven applications to their environments, the challenge may become less about deploying another security tool and more about creating a coherent way to manage what is already in place. Huskeys is betting that Network Edge Security Management can become that missing layer.

title: Walnut Launches Enterprise AI Agent Platform to Personalize the B2B Buyer Experience
partialText:
For B2B software companies, product-led buying has created a new challenge: buyers increasingly expect to explore products on their own terms, while go-to-market teams still have limited time to tailor those experiences. Walnut is now betting that AI can make that personalization scalable.

Walnut, a platform used by go-to-market teams at hundreds of B2B software companies, announced a family of AI agents designed to cover both sides of the buying experience. The company is introducing AI Mode for Playlists and Deal Rooms, which creates a personalized buyer-facing experience from a single prompt, and Walnut Xpert, an agent that allows buyers to ask questions and navigate a product demo according to their interests.

The two new agents join InsightsAI and AI Mode for demos, which are already available on the platform.

From High-Value Deals to Every Buyer

The shift Walnut is targeting is straightforward: personalization no longer has to be reserved for a company's largest opportunities.

According to Walnut, creating a personalized playlist or deal room previously took an account executive or customer success manager roughly three hours per deal. With AI Mode for Playlists and Deal Rooms, that process can now begin with a single sentence describing what a particular buyer needs.

The company says demo creation has undergone a similar transformation. Processes that previously took days, and later hours, have been reduced to minutes through Walnut's demo creation and personalization agents over the past year, while maintaining greater fidelity and interactivity.

On the buyer side, Walnut Xpert is designed to turn the demo itself into an interactive conversation. Buyers can ask questions, explore specific areas of a product and determine their own path through the experience instead of following a fixed click-through sequence.

Walnut says sessions using Xpert alongside a demo run more than twice as long as sessions without it. The questions buyers ask can also provide intent signals that a traditional static demo cannot capture, giving GTM teams visibility into what prospects actually want to understand.

One AI Architecture Across the Buying Journey

The foundation behind Walnut's agents is its product capture technology. Rather than generating product experiences from a prompt and an approximation of what software looks like, the company's system captures the actual product, including its screens, flows and data, and uses that context to build buyer-facing assets.

That same captured context is used across Walnut's agents. When AI Mode creates a demo or Walnut Xpert responds to a buyer's question, the output is grounded in what the product actually does.

The approach is intended to address a challenge that can emerge as companies adopt multiple AI tools: disconnected systems can produce disconnected messages. Walnut's model is designed so the demo, playlist, deal room and buyer interaction are built from a shared foundation.

"Every company has access to the same frontier models now, so the ability to build features isn't a competitive advantage anymore. What is: your ability to go to market effectively, tell a coherent story, and create a buyer experience that actually helps your buyer make the informed decision," said Oren Blank, CEO of Walnut.

Governance Before Autonomy

Walnut's expansion into AI agents also includes a governance layer. Before introducing autonomous capabilities, the company released the AI Center, which provides administrators with visibility, permissions and guardrails for AI use across their workspace.

The company says that sequencing is intentional. As agents take on more work on behalf of organizations, administrators need a centralized way to understand and control how those systems operate.

Walnut is also extending that governance model with bring-your-own-key (BYOK) support. The capability is intended to give customers direct control over security, privacy and spending while allowing Walnut's buyer-enablement architecture to work with different underlying models.

Making the Buyer Experience Interactive

AI Mode for Playlists and Deal Rooms combines captured product content, information from a buyer's CRM record and the seller's stated intent to assemble a personalized experience. The goal is to extend the story already established by the product demo rather than forcing sellers to construct a separate experience for every account.

Walnut Xpert takes the concept directly to the buyer. Instead of simply viewing a predefined demo, prospects can ask questions and explore the product with an agent grounded in the seller's captured product.

That interaction can also generate a more detailed record of buyer interest. Rather than relying primarily on signals such as clicks or page views, GTM teams can see what prospects actually asked about.

Walnut emphasizes that the agents do not replace the human decision about which story should be told. GTM teams determine the audience and narrative, while the agents execute against that direction using the shared product context.

Availability

The AI Center, AI Mode for demos, AI Mode for Playlists and Deal Rooms, and Walnut Xpert are available to Walnut customers today.

Walnut said BYOK support and a companion MCP, which will allow customers to run the platform through the AI provider of their choice, are expected to roll out in the coming weeks.

title: Zoomex Deepens TradFi Push With 50+ Stock Perpetuals and Zero-Fee TradFi
partialText:
VICTORIA/Seychelles/--Zoomex, a global cryptocurrency trading platform focused on derivatives trading, today confirmed that its Stock Perpetuals lineup has grown past 50 contracts, marking one of the most significant product expansions in the exchange's history.

The milestone consolidates Zoomex's position as a platform built for traders who want round-the-clock access to the world's most closely watched equities, without ever leaving the derivatives infrastructure they already trust and it lands just as the exchange kicks off a limited-time Zero-Fee TradFi event designed to let traders put that expanded lineup to work at no cost.

Source: Zoomex

The milestone consolidates Zoomex's position as a platform built for traders who want round-the-clock access to the world's most closely watched equities, without ever leaving the derivatives infrastructure they already trust.

50+ Contracts Across Four Asset Categories

The expansion spans four distinct categories of U.S. and global equities, all margined and settled in USDT: established mega-cap anchors including AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, and NVDA; a fast-growing AI and semiconductor cluster covering AMD, INTC, AVGO, ASML, ARM, MRVL, QCOM, and TXN; crypto-adjacent equities such as COIN, MSTR, MARA, RIOT, CIFR, and HOOD; and a broader healthcare, finance, and consumer segment featuring UNH, GE, JPM, GILD, REGN, AMGN, WMT, KO, PEP, MA, PYPL, and BRK.B. Each contract trades 24/7 with leverage of up to 25x on most pairs, giving traders continuous exposure to names that traditional brokerages close off for two-thirds of every week.

Source: Zoomex

Same Infrastructure, One Search Away

Easy to Use is the design principle running through the entire rollout. Rather than requiring a separate account, a different interface, or a new onboarding flow, every new Stock Perpetual contract runs on the same infrastructure as Zoomex's existing USDT Perpetuals. Traders simply search the ticker under the Stock category in Perpetual Trading and open a position the same way they would on any crypto pair, with no currency conversion, no international wire transfer, and no waiting for a market to reopen.

Source: Zoomex

That accessibility sits inside a broader industry shift. Tokenized stock perpetuals have moved from a niche experiment to one of the fastest-growing corners of crypto derivatives in 2026, as both retail and institutional traders look for leveraged, always-on access to equities that conventional exchanges gate behind fixed trading hours.

Zoomex's answer to that demand has been to build the category out methodically rather than opportunistically: the current 50+ contract lineup is the product of a sustained rollout throughout the year, not a single reactive listing event, and it now lives inside the exchange's newly unified TradFi Zone alongside Commodity Contracts and Stock Tokens.

Built on Transparency and Rule-Based Execution

Transparent by Design underpins how each contract is structured. Every Stock Perpetual on Zoomex carries clearly published fee schedules, funding rates, and margin requirements, with support for both cross and isolated margin modes depending on how a trader wants to manage risk. There are no hidden spreads and no ambiguity about how a position is priced relative to the underlying equity, an approach the exchange has extended from its crypto-native perpetuals lineup directly onto its equity products.

Fair Access & Rule-Based Execution defines the trading experience itself. Every Stock Perpetual is priced and matched through the same high-performance matching engine that underpins Zoomex's core derivatives stack, with consistent execution logic applied whether a trader is opening a position on NVDA at 3 a.m. Seychelles time or closing one on JPM during a U.S. market holiday. That consistency matters more for equities than for most crypto pairs, since the entire value proposition of a stock perpetual is that it behaves identically around the clock, with no gaps in liquidity or execution quality tied to when Wall Street happens to be open.

"Fifty contracts isn't just a number, it's a statement about where we think trading is headed," said Fernando Lillo, Marketing Director at Zoomex. "Traders no longer want to think in terms of separate accounts for crypto and equities, or separate hours for when each market is actually open to them. Focused on Derivatives has always meant giving people one infrastructure that can price and execute both, with the same rules applying no matter what's underneath the contract."

That single-infrastructure approach is also what makes the expansion Focused on Derivatives rather than a departure from Zoomex's core identity. The exchange has not pivoted away from crypto derivatives to chase equities; it has extended the same derivatives engine, matching logic, and risk controls that already serve its crypto perpetuals to a new asset class, letting traders build cross-asset strategies inside a single account rather than splitting exposure across multiple platforms and jurisdictions.

A Trust Framework That Scales With the Lineup

Underpinning all of it is the Refined Brand & Trading Experience Zoomex has built around verifiable trust. The exchange publishes regular Proof of Reserves data, undergoes independent security audits through Hacken, and maintains security transparency and regulatory compliance disclosures that traders can check directly rather than take on faith.

As the Stock Perpetuals lineup has grown, that same trust framework has scaled with it: reserves backing the platform's USDT-margined products are tracked and reported through the same on-chain transparency process Zoomex applies to its broader treasury, giving traders a way to verify that the infrastructure behind a 24/7 NVDA or COIN position is as accountable as the infrastructure behind its BTC or ETH pairs.

Zero-Fee TradFi Event Removes the Cost Barrier to Trying It

Timed directly to the 50-contract milestone, Zoomex has launched a TradFi Zero-Fee event running from August 28, 2026, 10:00 AM UTC through September 4, 2026, 10:00 AM UTC, giving traders a concrete, no-cost way to explore the newly consolidated TradFi Zone. The mechanics stay true to Transparent by Design: registration is required to participate, but traders who already signed up for the earlier TradFi Early Bird event are automatically carried over, with no re-registration needed.

Source: Zoomex

Once registered, any trade executed on a pair within the TradFi Zone, spanning Stock Contracts, Commodity Contracts, and Stock Tokens, including the freshly expanded Stock Perpetuals lineup, qualifies for a 100% rebate on trading fees actually paid, up to a cumulative cap of 100 USDT per user.

Rebates are calculated strictly on fees paid in real terms; amounts already covered or discounted through trial funds, fee-deduction vouchers, or other coupons don't count toward the rebate, and for Stock Tokens, on-chain gas costs are excluded as well. Approved rebates are credited to eligible accounts within seven business days of the event's close.

The structure reflects Fair Access & Rule-Based Execution in practice rather than just in messaging: the cap, the exclusions, and the settlement window are all published upfront, so traders know exactly what they're eligible for before they place a single order. Paired with a lineup that has just crossed 50 Stock Perpetuals, the event functions as an invitation to test the cross-asset TradFi Zone risk-free during the exact week the category's expansion is being announced, Easy to Use extended from product design into the promotion itself.

About Zoomex

Founded in 2021, Zoomex is a global cryptocurrency trading platform focused on derivatives trading. The platform serves over 3 million users across 35+ countries and regions, offering access to 700+ trading pairs. Built around easy to use, transparency, fairness, and speed, Zoomex provides a clear and efficient trading experience for users worldwide.

Through its high-performance matching engine, clear asset and order displays, and transparent fee and rule mechanisms, Zoomex helps users better understand their account status, order execution, trading costs, and results. Zoomex maintains registrations, licenses, and regulatory statuses across multiple jurisdictions, including the U.S. MSB, Canada MSB, U.S. NFA, and Australia AUSTRAC, and has completed security audits conducted by blockchain security firm Hacken. The platform also continues to strengthen its trust framework through Proof of Reserves, Security & Transparency, Compliance Information, and Fees / Rules Transparency initiatives.

Beyond trading, Zoomex builds a refined brand experience through elite sports partnerships, including the TGR Haas F1 Team, World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez, and world-class tennis events such as Wimbledon. The values of speed, precision, discipline, fair play, and rule-based execution are closely aligned with Zoomex’s approach to derivatives trading.

At Zoomex: Easy to Use. Transparent balance. Fair access to your earnings.
